builder_plan.scenario: Profiling shows attention computation is a bottleneck in your self-hosted service.
builder_plan.change: Check the supported GPU, tensor shapes, and precision, then replace only the relevant kernel.
builder_plan.baseline: The existing kernel inside the same complete serving pipeline.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Numerical differences, end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory at realistic shapes.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CompileMask: Bridging the Gap Between Expressiveness and Efficiency in Attention Masking
summary: It replaces predicate-based custom masking, which materializes or evaluates masks expensively, and fixed-count interval masking, which limits expressiveness, with an offline-compiled MaskSpec rule that emits a preprocess kernel and a compact Execution Descriptor for endpoint comparisons. The cost is an added compiler and DSL dependency, integration with a compatible attention kernel, an online preprocessing step that reads batch metadata, and engineering effort that is only justified when runtime-dependent masks are a measured bottleneck. It can fail when visibility rules are not reducible to region endpoints, when metadata changes in ways the descriptor cannot represent, when the target attention backend is unsupported, or when the workload uses standard causal or full masks and sees little benefit.
rationale: For a single-GPU or API-constrained team this is relevant only if self-hosted inference or fine-tuning is bottlenecked by diverse runtime-dependent attention masks, so it merits a small benchmark rather than immediate production adoption.

The cost is an added compiler and DSL dependency, integration with a compatible attention kernel, an online preprocessing step that reads batch metadata, and engineering effort that is only justified when runtime-dependent masks are a measured bottleneck. It can fail when visibility rules are not reducible to region endpoints, when metadata changes in ways the descriptor cannot represent, when the target attention backend is unsupported, or when the workload uses standard causal or full masks and sees little benefit.
Reports up to 3.8x speedup over state-of-the-art custom-mask attention methods; this is an upper-bound claim, not a guaranteed workload result.
